cards.title: Regrowth Interpretation and Resistance Mechanism Ambiguity
cards.claim: Regrowth after initial killing is a common observation in time-kill studies but does not uniquely identify the underlying resistance mechanism. It may result from the emergence of resistant subpopulations (genetic), phenotypic switching to a persister state, or drug depletion/degradation. In static models, regrowth can occur even at concentrations far exceeding clinically achievable levels, indicating that regrowth is not solely a function of sub-MIC exposure.
conditions: Applies to both static and dynamic in vitro PK/PD models.
Requires careful distinction between 'regrowth due to resistance' and 'regrowth due to drug loss'.
required_inputs: Control growth curves to establish baseline exponential growth.
Drug stability data to rule out degradation as the sole cause of regrowth.
Time-course data showing the transition from killing to regrowth.
limitations: Regrowth alone cannot distinguish between intrinsic, acquired, or adaptive resistance.
In vitro models lack immune system interactions, which may alter regrowth dynamics in vivo.
Abstract-only or partial data may obscure the specific mechanism driving regrowth.
cards.downstream_use: Do not infer a specific genetic resistance mechanism solely from regrowth patterns. Use additional data (e.g., MIC shifts, genetic sequencing) to characterize resistance. Use regrowth data to parameterize models that include both susceptible and resistant/persister states.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Time-kill, regrowth and resistance mechanism interpretation

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
